## Getting started
- [Getting Started Overview](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/overview.md): An introduction to the Nexudus Platform documentation and links to main sections.
- [What is Nexudus?](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/what-is-nexudus.md): Discover the Nexudus platform and its key benefits for coworking operators.
- [Who is this for?](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/who-is-this-for.md): Understand the intended audience for the Nexudus platform and its documentation.
- [Admin vs Members Portal](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/platform-overview/admin-vs-members-portal.md): Understand the differences between the Admin Panel and the Members Portal in the Nexudus platform.
- [Understanding Your Nexudus Platform Data Structure](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/platform-overview/data-model-overview.md): Learn how data is organized and connected in Nexudus to optimize coworking operations.
- [How Admin Settings Affect Members](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/platform-overview/how-configuration-flows-to-members.md): Understand how configuration and data flow from the Admin Panel to the Members Portal, shaping the user experience.
### Quick Starts
- [Configure your Location](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/quick-starts/configure-location.md): Set up your coworking space location details in Nexudus to enable members to see accurate information about your facility
- [Configure Opening Hours](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/quick-starts/opening-hours.md): Set your location's operating hours and manage booking availability exceptions in Nexudus
- [Set up Resources Inventory](https://learn.nexudus.com/get-started/quick-starts/set-resources-inventory.md): Configure your resources and floor plans to enable members to book spaces in your coworking location
- [Stripe Checkout](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/payment-gateways/stripe-checkout.md): How to connect Stripe Checkout so customers can pay by card, wallet or bank debit, including Apple Pay setup.
- [Access control](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/overview.md): Connect your door access system to Nexudus, so customers get and lose door access automatically from their passes, bookings and contracts, and door unlocks can check them in.
- [ACT365](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/act365.md): Connect ACT365 cloud access control to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their cards based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and door unlocks check them in.
- [Avigilon](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/avigilon.md): Connect an on-premise Avigilon Access Control Manager to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their cards and PIN based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Avigilon Alta](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/avigilon-alta.md): Connect Avigilon Alta (formerly OpenPath) to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their card or phone based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and visitors get a CloudKey link.
- [Brivo](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/brivo.md): Connect Brivo cloud access control to Nexudus, so customers and visitors open doors based on their passes, bookings and contracts, with Brivo Mobile Pass on their phone.
- [DoorFlow](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/doorflow.md): Connect DoorFlow cloud access control to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their PIN, card, fob or the DoorFlow app based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Gallagher](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/gallagher.md): Connect Gallagher Command Centre to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their cards or PIN based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and zone access checks them in.
- [Genetec](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/genetec.md): Connect Genetec Security Center to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their card or PIN based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Paxton Net2](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/paxton-net2.md): Connect Paxton Net2 to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their cards and fobs based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Salto KS](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/saltov2.md): Connect Salto KS cloud access control to Nexudus, so customers open doors with tags or their phone based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and visitors get a PIN.
- [SofiaLocks](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/sofialocks.md): Connect SofiaLocks smart locks to Nexudus, so customers and visitors open doors with their phone based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and door opens check them in.
- [UniFi Access](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/unifi-access.md): Connect Ubiquiti UniFi Access to Nexudus through the Network Bridge, so customers open doors with their NFC card, PIN or phone based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [MikroTik](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/wifi/mikrotik.md): Use a MikroTik router as a Wi-Fi hotspot with a Nexudus captive portal, so customers sign in with their Nexudus details and are checked in automatically.
- [Calendly](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/scheduling/calendly.md): Use a Calendly event to schedule tours, so people booking a tour on your members portal pick a time in Calendly.
- [Analytics](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/analytics.md): Track your members portal with Google Analytics 4 or Google Tag Manager, send your data to Google BigQuery, and build reports with Nexudus Explore.
- [Google Analytics](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/google-analytics.md): Track how customers browse and purchase on your Members Portal using Google Analytics 4 or Google Tag Manager.
- [Google Tag Manager](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/analytics/google-tag-manager.md): Add your Google Tag Manager container to every page of your members portal.
- [Google BigQuery](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/analytics/google-bigquery.md): Copy your Nexudus customers, invoices, bookings, contracts and more to Google BigQuery in real time for your own reporting.
- [Website and portal](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/website.md): Protect your members portal forms with reCAPTCHA, show maps with Google Maps, and validate email addresses with Verifalia.
- [reCAPTCHA](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/website/recaptcha.md): Protect your members portal sign-up and contact forms from spam and abuse with Google reCAPTCHA.
- [Google Maps](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/website/google-maps.md): Show your location on a map on your members portal and in the app, with address autocomplete.
- [Verifalia](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/website/verifalia.md): Check email addresses are real in real time when customers sign up or admins add them.
- [Workplace and building](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/workplace.md): Import floor plans from Archilogic, run Smartalock lockers, connect CMS Engage workplace technology, and show a live space dashboard.
- [Archilogic](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/workplace/archilogic.md): Import floor plan models from Archilogic into Nexudus to use as your floor plans.
## Member Portal
- [Member Portal Overview](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/overview.md): A guide to all the sections and pages your members see in the Nexudus Members Portal.
- [URL Parameters Reference](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/url-parameters.md): A complete reference of URL parameters you can use to deep-link into specific Members Portal pages with pre-filled values.
- [Home Page](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/home.md): The landing page of your Members Portal — hero section, plans, featured events, and locations.
- [Resource List](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/resource-list.md): How members browse, filter, and book meeting rooms and desks in the Members Portal.
- [Events](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/events.md): How members browse, filter, and view events in the Members Portal.
- [Courses](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/courses.md): How members browse courses and view course content, lessons, and enrollment information.
- [Articles](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/articles.md): How members browse articles, read content, and engage through comments.
- [Tours](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/tours.md): How visitors request and book tours of your coworking space through the Members Portal.
- [Contact Us](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/contact.md): The contact page where visitors can reach your coworking space.
- [Community Board](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/community-board.md): The discussion forum where members post topics and interact with each other.
- [Members Directory](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/directory.md): A searchable directory where members showcase their professional profiles.
- [Perks](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/perks.md): Member perks, benefits, and partner offers displayed in the portal.
- [Automation Tiles](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/automation-tiles.md): How automation tiles let customers perform actions by scanning a QR code or tapping an NFC tile in the Members Portal.
### Checkout / Purchase Flows
- [Booking Checkout](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/booking-checkout.md): The booking checkout flow where members create or edit resource bookings.
- [Dynamic Pricing](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/dynamic-pricing.md): How dynamic pricing adjusts booking costs based on demand, availability, and last-minute bookings — and how members see it in the portal.
- [Store](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/store.md): The browsable product catalogue where members discover and select products.
- [Product Checkout](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/product-checkout.md): The checkout page for purchasing a single product.
- [Event Checkout](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/event-checkout.md): The checkout flow for purchasing event tickets.
- [Course Checkout](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/course-checkout.md): The checkout flow for enrolling in a course.
- [Cart](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/cart.md): The multi-item shopping cart where customers review, manage, and check out multiple items at once.
- [Guest Checkout](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/guest-checkout.md): How guest checkout works and when it is available to customers who are not logged in.
- [Guest Invoice Payment](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/checkout/guest-invoice-payment.md): How to send a payment link for an existing invoice so customers can pay without logging in.

- [ACT365](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/act365.md): Connect ACT365 cloud access control to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their cards based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and door unlocks check them in.
- [Avigilon](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/avigilon.md): Connect an on-premise Avigilon Access Control Manager to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their cards and PIN based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Avigilon Alta](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/avigilon-alta.md): Connect Avigilon Alta (formerly OpenPath) to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their card or phone based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and visitors get a CloudKey link.
- [Brivo](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/brivo.md): Connect Brivo cloud access control to Nexudus, so customers and visitors open doors based on their passes, bookings and contracts, with Brivo Mobile Pass on their phone.
- [DoorFlow](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/doorflow.md): Connect DoorFlow cloud access control to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their PIN, card, fob or the DoorFlow app based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Gallagher](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/gallagher.md): Connect Gallagher Command Centre to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their cards or PIN based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and zone access checks them in.
- [Genetec](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/genetec.md): Connect Genetec Security Center to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their card or PIN based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Paxton Net2](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/paxton-net2.md): Connect Paxton Net2 to Nexudus, so customers open doors with their cards and fobs based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Salto KS](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/saltov2.md): Connect Salto KS cloud access control to Nexudus, so customers open doors with tags or their phone based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and visitors get a PIN.
- [SofiaLocks](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/sofialocks.md): Connect SofiaLocks smart locks to Nexudus, so customers and visitors open doors with their phone based on their passes, bookings and contracts, and door opens check them in.
- [UniFi Access](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/access-control/unifi-access.md): Connect Ubiquiti UniFi Access to Nexudus through the Network Bridge, so customers open doors with their NFC card, PIN or phone based on their passes, bookings and contracts.
- [Google BigQuery](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/analytics/google-bigquery.md): Copy your Nexudus customers, invoices, bookings, contracts and more to Google BigQuery in real time for your own reporting.
- [reCAPTCHA](https://learn.nexudus.com/integrations/website/recaptcha.md): Protect your members portal sign-up and contact forms from spam and abuse with Google reCAPTCHA.
- [📆Book resource](https://learn.nexudus.com/rest-api/apps/post-marketplaceapplications-2.md): Creates a booking for a given resource, start date and duration.
- [📆Update resource booking](https://learn.nexudus.com/rest-api/apps/put-marketplaceapplications-2.md): Updates a booking for a given resource, start date and duration.

18-## Booking pages
19-
20-### Resource list and calendar
21-
22-**Path:** `/bookings/:type/:view`
23-
24-Use this to send customers directly to a filtered view of bookable resources.
25-
26-| Parameter | Location | Description |
27-| - | - | - |
28-| `:type` | Path | Resource type slug (e.g. `meeting-rooms`, `hot-desks`, `all`) |
29:| `:view` | Path | View mode: `list`, `calendar`, `map`, or `floorplan` |
30:| `start` | Query | Start date/time in ISO 8601 format (e.g. `2026-06-01T09:00:00`) |
31-| `end` | Query | End date/time in ISO 8601 format |
32-| `view` | Query | Calendar sub-view: `day`, `week`, `month`, or `list` |
33-| `type` | Query | Filter by resource type ID |
34-| `group` | Query | Filter by resource group name |
35-| `Allocation` | Query | Minimum capacity (number of persons) |
36:| `floorplan_id` | Query | Floor plan ID (for the floorplan view) |
37-| `customFields` | Query | Comma-separated custom field filters |

40-
41-`Projector`, `Internet`, `ConferencePhone`, `StandardPhone`, `WhiteBoard`, `LargeDisplay`, `Catering`, `TeaAndCoffee`, `Drinks`, `SecurityLock`, `CCTV`, `VoiceRecorder`, `AirConditioning`, `Heating`, `NaturalLight`, `StandingDesk`, `QuietZone`, `WirelessCharger`, `PrivacyScreen`

content.text:
You were right: my earlier fix doesn't work. There's no plan setting for this. Hacker Dojo's members portal hardcodes the default start date to tomorrow.

**What causes it**
- The checkout page (`hackerdojo.nexudus.site/checkout/tariffs`) sets the start date to `?start=` from the URL if present. Otherwise it uses `now().startOf("day").plus({day:1})`, which is tomorrow. Nexudus doesn't expose a setting for it.
- A contract that starts tomorrow stays `Active:false` until Nexudus's nightly job at about 07:02 UTC (midnight Pacific). `syncd` only admits active contracts, so the member gets WiFi at about 07:05 UTC.
- Members can still change the date to today in the date picker. A few did: those contracts went active within a minute and synced right away.

**When it started:** from 300 contracts, February to August were nearly all same-day starts. Next-day starts take over from about 2026-09-17, and in October 17 of 22 contracts start the next day or later. My guess is that's when the Dojo moved to the v5 portal (now on the `nexudus.site` domain), but I couldn't confirm the date of that switch.

**Fix options (your call; it affects who gets WiFi):**
1. **Admit pending contracts in nexudus-radius (my recommendation).** Also count contracts that are inactive and not cancelled, where the customer is active and `StartDate` is within about 36 hours. This doesn't depend on Nexudus or on how people reach the signup page. The trade-off is that WiFi works a few hours before the contract starts. About 1–2 hours with tests.
2. **Fix the signup link.** Point the Dojo's "Join" link at a redirect that adds `?start=<today in Pacific>`. It only helps people who come in through that link, not anyone who browses to the plans page directly.
3. **Report it to Nexudus.** Defaulting to tomorrow is arguably a bug. It's worth doing alongside 1 or 2, but you can't count on them to fix it quickly.

The temporary credential file, contract dump and downloaded portal code have been deleted. Two of the API calls printed one member's name and email to this session; nothing was written to disk.

**Next action (~1 min):** reply "1", "2", or "1+3" and I'll start on it.

Sources:
- [Nexudus portal URL parameters (`/checkout/tariffs?start=`)](https://learn.nexudus.com/member-portal/public/url-parameters.md)
- [Nexudus Contracts: future-dated contracts activate when the start date is reached](https://help.nexudus.com/docs/contracts)
- [Understanding Contract Dates](https://help.nexudus.com/docs/understanding-contract-dates)
- [Joining Plans](https://help.nexudus.com/docs/joining-plans)
- [Nexudus product updates](https://nexudus.com/product-updates/)
- [Introducing the new Members Portal](https://nexudus.com/product-update/introducing-the-new-members-portal/)
- [Members Portal Version 5 FAQ](https://help.nexudus.com/docs/members-portal-version-5-faq)

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/tdd

# TDD

## Overview

**Test-first, always.** Write the failing test before the code it covers, watch
it fail, then write the minimal code to make it pass. A test you never saw fail
proves nothing — it may pass for the wrong reason, or not exercise the behavior
at all.

Keep the test scoped to the interfaces you are actually changing — a test that
drifts wider stops being a contract anyone can rely on. Inside a drovr phase
this also binds the next phase's contract.

## The cycle

1. **RED** — write the failing test named in the task's verification. Run it.
   *Watch it fail*, and confirm it fails for the reason you expect (missing
   behavior, not a typo or compile error elsewhere).
2. **GREEN** — write the *minimal* code to make that test pass. No extra
   features, no speculative abstraction — just enough to go green.
3. **REFACTOR** — clean up with the test as your safety net, re-running it.

Repeat per behavior. One failing test at a time.

## Red flags — STOP

- Wrote code before the test → delete it, start with the test.
- "I'll add the test after" → tests-after check *what the code does*, not what it
  *should* do. Test first.
- Test passed the first time you ran it → you never saw RED; make sure it truly
  exercises the new behavior.
- Test is scoped wider than this task's interfaces → tighten it; drift breaks the

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/tdd

# TDD

## Overview

**Test-first, always.** Write the failing test before the code it covers, watch
it fail, then write the minimal code to make it pass. A test you never saw fail
proves nothing — it may pass for the wrong reason, or not exercise the behavior
at all.

Keep the test scoped to the interfaces you are actually changing — a test that
drifts wider stops being a contract anyone can rely on. Inside a drovr phase
this also binds the next phase's contract.

## The cycle

1. **RED** — write the failing test named in the task's verification. Run it.
   *Watch it fail*, and confirm it fails for the reason you expect (missing
   behavior, not a typo or compile error elsewhere).
2. **GREEN** — write the *minimal* code to make that test pass. No extra
   features, no speculative abstraction — just enough to go green.
3. **REFACTOR** — clean up with the test as your safety net, re-running it.

Repeat per behavior. One failing test at a time.

## Red flags — STOP

- Wrote code before the test → delete it, start with the test.
- "I'll add the test after" → tests-after check *what the code does*, not what it
  *should* do. Test first.
- Test passed the first time you ran it → you never saw RED; make sure it truly
  exercises the new behavior.
- Test is scoped wider than this task's interfaces → tighten it; drift breaks the
  contract the next phase inherits.

## Verifying the pass

Green on the one test is necessary, not sufficient. Before claiming done, hand
off to `drovr:verification-before-completion` — run the full suite and the build,
and confirm with evidence, not assertion.
Using drovr:tdd: red test first. I'll track the steps in a scratch checklist, since this harness has no task tool. Surveying the repo layout first:

// Package nexudus is a minimal read-only client for the Nexudus REST API.
package nexudus

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// Pin is a customer's access PIN. Nexudus documents it as a string, but it
// is decoded leniently so a numeric or null value does not break a sync.
type Pin string

func (p *Pin) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error {
	s := strings.TrimSpace(string(b))
	if s == "null" {
		*p = ""
		return nil
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(s, `"`) {
		var v string
		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &v); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("AccessPincode: %w", err)
		}
		*p = Pin(strings.TrimSpace(v))
		return nil
	}
	var n json.Number
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &n); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("AccessPincode: %w", err)
	}
	*p = Pin(n.String())
	return nil
}

// Coworker is a Nexudus customer. AccessPincode is only populated by
// GetCoworker; listings leave it empty.
type Coworker struct {
	ID            int64  `json:"Id"`
	Email         string `json:"Email"`
	Active        bool   `json:"Active"`
	AccessPincode Pin    `json:"AccessPincode"`
	UpdatedOn     string `json:"UpdatedOn"`
}

content.content:
syncd waits about five minutes between syncs, and not the same five as its neighbour
Three syncds on one Nexudus account started within three seconds of each
other and synced on a fixed two-minute ticker, so they called Nexudus at the
same moment every time. Nexudus answered some of them 429 on the first
request of the pass; one pod lost nine passes in a row after a rollout and
was unready for nineteen minutes.

The default interval is 5m. Each wait is somewhere from four fifths to six
fifths of it, so pods started together drift apart. After a failed pass the
wait is a fifth of that, because a pod is not ready until its first sync.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

WIFI_SECURITY goes: the files are made for a WPA3-only network
There is no setting for the network's kind any more. What the setting
gave with "wpa3" is now what every deployment gets: the Apple profile
says WPA3, the Linux file and command require protected management
frames, the settings to type in by hand say WPA3-Enterprise, and the
page points older devices to the "(Legacy)" network. The two Windows
files say WPA2, as of the commit before.

content.content: Launching skill: drovr:code-review

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/code-review

# Code Review

## Overview

**They find, you fix.** Follow the spirit, not the letter: dispatching a
reviewer satisfies the letter; one that read an empty diff, or that you never
waited for, looked at nothing and found nothing. The rule is that
somebody who did not write the change has said what is wrong with it — and that
cannot be you. You read the change you meant to make, not the one on disk.

**Write for the agent who inherits this: the next phase agent is you, with your
context gone.** A finding you settled in your head is one they meet as a bug,
with nothing saying anyone saw it.

## The Iron Law

```
NO CHANGE IS DONE UNTIL A READ-ONLY REVIEWER HAS SEEN IT AND
EVERY CRITICAL AND IMPORTANT FINDING IS RESOLVED OR RECORDED AS DEFERRED.
```

**Read-only** is a trust boundary, not a performance note: the reviewer reads
anything, runs read-only checks, and writes nothing — not source, not git, not
run state. You stay the single writer.

No exceptions. The first names its addressee; the rest hold for anyone.

- **Never run a reviewer in the background — you, the agent in a herdr pane,
  where ending a turn *is* how you report done.** Do not set
  `run_in_background`, do not yield, and do not schedule a wakeup while one is
  out. A backgrounded reviewer parks you mid-turn, indistinguishable from a
  finished turn, and the run stalls until a human nudges the pane. Dispatch it
  blocking and read its verdict in the turn you dispatched it. That reason is
  role-specific, so there is exactly one role it does not bind: a **driver**
  reviewing its own inline change, which may background the panel and end the
  turn because its harness re-invokes it on process exit. Inside a pipeline
  run the driver has no panel to background — the task agent's is the gate,
  and `skills/pipeline/SKILL.md` says so at its own loop. In a pane, the
  prohibition is yours.
- **Do not judge a change too small to review.** A one-line edit to a condition
  is the size this skill exists for. Dispatch a reviewer over it.
- **Do not count your own read as the review.** Re-reading your diff tells you
  it matches what you intended — the one thing never in doubt. Dispatch someone
  who does not know it.
- **Do not leave it for the pipeline's review phase.** That phase reads what you
  hand it, after later work is built on it. Dispatch here, while the change is
  one commit wide.
- **Do not close a finding by disagreeing with it.** When you will not fix one,
  quote it and write the reason in the report or handoff. An unrecorded
  decision reads downstream like an unread finding.
- **Do not repeat a verdict you have not read.** Open the file the reviewer
  names, or re-run the review when it named none. A reviewer that never came
  back has not said "clean".

content.content:
---
name: drovr-review-panel-drops-angles
description: "drovr code-review rounds randomly lose an angle to reviewer-model degeneration; don't read it as a finding or re-run indefinitely"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a23b43bd-baa0-42ff-8956-8df3eaad4ff7
  modified: 2026-09-30T05:45:00.000Z
---

`drovr code-review run` in this repo drops a random angle roughly half the time.
The reviewer model (`google/gemma-4-31b-it`, pinned in `opencode.nix` as
`small_model`) degenerates into printing `a- a- a- a-` until the response is
truncated, writes no findings file, and drovr records the angle as an
undelivered Critical. On 2026-09-29 a single unchanged commit took 5 rounds:
clean, lost error-handling, clean, lost error-handling, lost security.

**Why:** the skill's termination rule ("two consecutive clean rounds over an
unchanged HEAD") can't be reached when the panel alternates, so the obvious
reading — re-run until clean twice — burns rounds measuring nothing. The
Critical is about the panel, not the code.

**How to apply:** a lost angle is infra, not a finding — don't try to fix the
diff in response to it. The skill's third exit exists for this: two
*consecutive* rounds that lost a dimension ends the loop on a record rather than
a verdict. Say which angles never ran. If every angle has delivered clean at
least once over the identical HEAD, that is the real evidence; stop there rather
than chasing the pair. Changing the reviewer model off `small_model` would fix
it at the source.

**When the lost angle is `correctness`, substitute a real reviewer rather than
settling for the record.** On 2026-09-30 the panel lost correctness twice
consecutively on the elephant/walker fix while the other three came back clean.
Dispatching the read-only `Explore` subagent with an explicit skeptical
correctness brief (name the claims, tell it to verify rather than trust, demand
Critical/Important/nit ratings) returned four Important findings in ~12 min —
including that the commit's central rationale was false and the machine's own
journal disproved it. The gemma panel had produced nothing on that angle across
two rounds. `explore-mcp` is not exposed in every session; `Explore` is, and it
cannot write, so single-writer holds.

Related: [[dotfiles-master-moves-under-you]]

You are a skeptical, READ-ONLY correctness reviewer. You did not write this change. Do not edit anything, do not run git commands that write, do not call any network service.

Repo worktree: /home/sauyon/devel/nexudus-radius/.claude/worktrees/pending-contracts
Change under review: `git diff 98da33d..3420369` (5 files: README.md, internal/nexudus/client.go, internal/nexudus/client_test.go, internal/syncer/syncer.go, internal/syncer/syncer_test.go). Read the whole diff and the surrounding code (internal/members, internal/store, cmd/syncd, test/e2e/fakenexudus).

Context: syncd mirrors Nexudus members into SQLite for FreeRADIUS. Previously only customers holding an ACTIVE contract got WiFi. Nexudus's v5 members portal defaults a new contract's start date to tomorrow (midnight local, America/Los_Angeles), and Nexudus flips Active=true only in an overnight job (~00:02 PT). The change adds a second query: contracts with CoworkerContract_Active=false, CoworkerContract_Cancelled=false, issued by the business, with from_/to_CoworkerContract_StartDate in [now-1h, now+24h] (formatted UTC "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z"), and unions those coworker IDs with the active holders.

Claims made by the author, to VERIFY not trust:
1. A portal-default "tomorrow" start is always within the 24h window, regardless of what time of day the signup happens (consider DST transitions too).
2. The union cannot drop anyone who was previously admitted (no regression for existing members), and errors in the new call abort the sync without touching the store.
3. The merge does not mutate maps returned by the API (fakes reuse them across syncs).
4. The tests would fail if the new behaviour regressed (e.g. if the starting IDs were ignored, or the window bounds changed).
5. The e2e fake (test/e2e/fakenexudus) still behaves sensibly given it ignores query params.

Also hunt for anything else: interplay with the mass-removal guard, PIN caching by UpdatedOn, members whose contract never activates, lapsed members renewing, a contract that ends and a new one starting, README accuracy vs code.

Rate every finding Critical, Important, or nit, with file:line and a concrete failure scenario. If you find none at a severity, say so explicitly. Say whether the tests actually exercise the behaviour. Return your findings as your final message (you cannot write files).

The doc comment on `members.Eligible` (`internal/members/members.go`) also still says "holding an active contract".

The listing only lets people on early, so when it fails the sync goes

content.text:
Option 1 is built, tested and reviewed on branch `pending-contracts` in nexudus-radius (2 commits). It isn't merged or deployed yet. Live Nexudus is still at 172 members. In my one-off test run against the live account, the new build admitted 175: the 3 customers whose contracts start tomorrow. One of them signed up at 17:50 PDT tonight, so under the current build they'd wait until about midnight.

**What changed**
- **Who gets on early:** `syncd` also lets on anyone whose contract isn't active yet, isn't cancelled, and starts within the next 25 hours. That person stays on for up to an hour after the start date while Nexudus activates the contract overnight.
- **Safety checks added after review:**
  - The start date and cancelled status are checked again in our code, so a filter Nexudus ignores can't let ended contracts back in.
  - If this new lookup fails, the sync carries on with active contracts only instead of failing.
  - The window is 25 hours rather than 24 so the day the clocks go back is covered.
- **Docs:** the README's "Who gets access" section explains the new rule.

**Checks run**
- The full Go test suite and `go vet` pass, and the new tests failed before the code existed.
- Against live Nexudus: contracts starting 10-20 and 10-30 were correctly left out.
- Review: two clean rounds from the four-reviewer panel on the final commit, plus a separate skeptical reviewer. That reviewer found three important issues; I fixed two. I rejected the third, that Nexudus might compare start dates in local time, because the live run showed it compares them in UTC, and I recorded why.

Deploying is up to you, since it means pushing to the public GitHub repo:
1. Merge `pending-contracts` into `main` and push. CI builds `sha-<commit>` images on ghcr.
2. Update the three image tags (currently `sha-98da33d`) in `charts/nexudus-radius/values.yaml` in the kube repo and push. ArgoCD then rolls it out.

**Next action:** reply "ship it" and I'll merge, push and update the image tags.
